Bright, friendly, slightly humorous; clear readable shapes; story reads from left to right.
Scene: A wide picture split into two eras by a soft glowing time-portal arch in the middle. LEFT ERA (ancient): a sunny ancient Roman-style building site; workers in simple tunics mix a pale paste in a wooden trough from a pile of white lime and a pile of dark grey volcanic ash; behind them rises a big round domed temple under construction with a round open hole (oculus) at the top of the dome, wooden scaffolding around it. RIGHT ERA (1820s England): a small brick workshop yard with a little bottle-shaped brick kiln giving off smoke; a generic 19th-century bricklayer in a cap and apron (not a portrait of any real person) grinds burnt lumps into grey powder; through the yard gate we see a grey sea and a rocky island cliff of pale cream building stone.
Characters:
  a chibi scientist with thin teal rectangular glasses, black hair with one white streak and a short tied-back ponytail, white lab coat over a black vest and tie, in the middle as a time-travel tour guide holding an old brass lantern, pointing from left to right;
  a girl researcher with long pink hair in two round buns and a navy streak, blue eyes, lavender hoodie under a white lab coat, jeans, on the right holding a small grey hardened cement block up next to a pale cream stone, comparing their colors with delighted eyes.
The one idea a student must get at a glance: the grey hardened cement looks just like the pale building stone from the island — that is where the name came from; people have glued stones since ancient times.
Composition: keep every important element large and clearly separated; simple background; nothing important touching the edges; leave a little calm space at the top.

Scene: A left-to-right 'time strip' in three stages. STAGE 1 (left, long ago): an underwater sea floor in soft blue-green, with seashells, corals, sea snails and tiny plankton slowly sinking and piling up into white layers. STAGE 2 (middle): the layers pressed into thick horizontal bands of pale rock, shown as a cross-section like a layered cake, with the sea now gone. STAGE 3 (right, today): a pale grey quarry cliff with stepped benches, a small yellow excavator, and a conveyor belt running a short distance to a cement plant right next to the quarry. Bottom right: four material heaps in a row on the ground — one HUGE pale-grey limestone heap (about four times bigger than the rest), a small brown clay heap, a small light silica-sand heap, a small rust-red iron-ore heap.

The one idea a student must get at a glance: most of cement starts as ancient sea creatures' shells turned into limestone; the plant sits right next to the quarry because limestone is the biggest ingredient.

Scene: A large cutaway (sliced-open) view of a very long, slightly tilted rotating steel kiln tube that runs across the whole picture from upper left (cool end) to lower right (hot end). The inside of the tube shows powder tumbling and rolling down. The inside color changes gradually along the tube to show temperature zones: pale blue at the upper-left entrance where tiny water droplets float up as steam; yellow in the middle where small grey bubbles (carbon dioxide puffs) rise out of the powder; deep orange; and finally white-hot at the lower-right end next to a big roaring burner flame. At the hot end, the powder has turned into dark grey marbles (clinker) that drop into a cooler box underneath where big fans blow light blue cool air on them. The outer shell of the kiln rests on big ring rollers.
Characters:
  a chibi scientist with thin teal rectangular glasses, black hair with one white streak and a short tied-back ponytail, white lab coat over a black vest and tie, standing in the lower left foreground holding a long pointer, explaining like a museum guide;
  a girl researcher with long pink hair in two round buns and a navy streak, blue eyes, lavender hoodie under a white lab coat, jeans, peeking through a round inspection window on the kiln with goggles on her forehead, amazed.
The one idea a student must get at a glance: a journey inside the kiln: first the water leaves, then carbon dioxide leaves, then at the hottest point the powder becomes marbles that must be cooled quickly.
Composition: keep every important element large and clearly separated; simple background; nothing important touching the edges; leave a little calm space at the top.

All four characters together:

  girl researcher, long pink hair with two round buns and a navy streak, blue eyes, white lab coat over lavender hoodie, jeans, beside the easel raising one index finger to explain;
  anthropomorphic fruit fly researcher, black body, big red compound eyes, blue helmet with a gold stripe and pink and blue cables, white lab coat over a black vest, black gloves, transparent wings, on the left facing right, pointing at the sketches with one eye narrowed;
  boxy beige retro CRT-monitor robot, dark green screen face with mint pixel eyes and mouth, short antenna topped with a red-brown abacus bead, gray segmented arms, two small tank treads, on the right facing left, holding up a wooden abacus.
Visual metaphor of the topic: thin beams of light flow from the six slots of the board into the three matching sketches, without any text.
Composition: keep every face and hand inside the central safe area (12% margin left and right, 10% top, 18% bottom); keep the bottom-left corner dark and simple; the light falls on the easel.

Match the art style, proportions and colors of the attached reference images exactly (if there are no reference images: 16-bit RPG style pixel art, bold dark outline, 2-3 tone shading, small highlights).

The same lecture room. A long horizontal ruler-like number line runs across the board with one zero mark glowing red. Match the art style, proportions and colors of the attached reference images exactly (if there are no reference images: 16-bit RPG style pixel art, bold dark outline, 2–3 tone shading, small highlights). Cozy night laboratory mood, purple light, soft magenta and green fluorescent accents, with warm golden lamp light in this room. Scene: cozy accounting room beside the lab, a giant wooden abacus on the back wall, thick sales record books with blank striped pages, a round vault door, a brass scale; on a long wooden desk a very long strip of sales record pages is unrolled from left to right, one blank striped cell per day, and two empty wooden picture frames ride on a thin brass rail above it — a short frame placed near the start of the strip and a long frame placed much further along. All four characters together: chibi scientist, thin teal rectangular glasses, spiky black hair with one white streak, small ponytail at the back, white lab coat over black vest and tie, standing in the center back holding a small brass scale in one hand and glancing from one frame to the other; girl researcher, long pink hair with two round buns and a navy streak, blue eyes, white lab coat over lavender hoodie, jeans, standing at the back left side opening a thick leather sales record and turning a page; anthropomorphic fruit fly researcher, black body, big red compound eyes, blue helmet with a gold stripe and pink and blue cables, white lab coat over a black vest, black gloves, transparent wings, on the left facing right, pushing the short frame one step along the rail; boxy beige retro CRT-monitor robot, dark green screen face with mint pixel eyes and mouth, short antenna topped with a red-brown abacus bead, gray segmented arms, two small tank treads, on the right facing left, standing beside the long frame and flicking a bead on a wooden abacus with one arm. Height ratio: scientist 1.00, girl 0.90, robot 0.72 including treads and antenna, fruit fly 0.41. Visual metaphor of the topic: a short window and a long window looking back over the same daily sales record, the long one starting later, without any text. Composition: keep every face and hand inside the central safe area (12% margin left and right, 10% top, 18% bottom); keep the bottom-left corner dark and simple; the light falls on the sales record strip and the two frames. Mood: curious, friendly rivalry, the moment before the result. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no weapons, no cigarettes, no alcohol, no blood, no real brands.
